scope: Explicit caller-supplied ASCII US English word break entries in one-run, left-aligned or justified, one-page ordinary managed PDF. A visible glyph outline and invisible original-word carrier retain searchable text but have a diagnosed first-line-only search highlight. Justified output also retains an independently observed geometry failure. This working-tree observation does not establish all #164 combinations.
provenance: Synthetic python-docx 1.2.0 (MIT) document with normalized ZIP metadata, independently regenerated byte for byte. The selected ex-tra-or-di-nary break points were independently checked using Pyphen 0.17.2 and its BSD-style US English hyphenation data (hyph_en_US.dic SHA-256 486fb6840b1049d5d252ef784be11cd4dc2be0bf296568b74b41e4f4e17cba7d); that dictionary is test-only and is not bundled by the library. Open XML SDK 3.5.1 reported zero errors for both source and saved DOCX.
independentChecks: Pyphen returned offsets 2, 5, 7 and 9; the visible break was after offset 7. Poppler pdftotext, pypdf 6.10.0 and PyMuPDF 1.27.2.2 each recovered the original word without an inserted hyphen after whitespace normalization. fontTools compared the painted hyphen outline to the actual embedded Noto Sans glyph at 0.05 pt; the observed size was 2.662 by 0.858 pt. Changed editable text and removed PDF content were independently rejected.
retainedEarlierAttempts: A separate raw PDF with ActualText over a visible hyphen caused pypdf to extract the display hyphen even though Poppler honored the replacement; this led to a visible outline and a separate original-text carrier. The first implementation builds encountered CA1711, CA1510, CA1845, CA2249, CA1847 and CA1861 analyzer errors; public naming, argument checks, concatenation and test fixtures were corrected. The unqualified search highlight remains diagnosed rather than treated as parity. The initial default-output control built two probes concurrently and one MSBuild process reported MSB4166 after child nodes exited; no failure details survived in the named temporary directory. A serial one-worker rebuild and rerun succeeded and the outputs matched. Source review found that trailing whitespace alone could trigger an unnecessary break and that an extremely narrow all-space token could enter an empty-word path; both cases now have explicit regression tests.
limitations: The checked specimens are synthetic and do not establish live Word, screen-reader or universal extractor behavior. The justified reference exceeds the original geometry tolerance. Authored soft hyphens, non-ASCII dictionaries, structured owners, native/tagged/archive output, preview, multiple physical pages and general #164 acceptance remain open. Exact-commit, package and hosted runtime evidence are separate.
tools: Poppler pdftotext 25.03.0; fontTools 4.61.1; pypdf 6.10.0; PyMuPDF 1.27.2.2; Pyphen 0.17.2; Open XML SDK 3.5.1.

defaultOutputControl.result: With the lexicon omitted and a fixed clock, the independent source produced byte-identical PDFs on the parent and working tree.

justifiedReference.producer: python-docx 1.2.0 generated the reference DOCX twice byte-identically with explicit US English soft break points; LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 ran offline in image sha256:a3aaef646226d406fc2b511462beb0359f4cd8859d775f404bd8f137dfd5f644 with the same Noto Sans font.
justifiedReference.result: The original word remained searchable in Poppler, pypdf and PyMuPDF, and justification moved the visible prefix to the line end. The original 0.5-point reference bound failed for the word origin and following-line top. The converter reports Hyphenation.JustificationApproximation and Strict rejects the pre-existing search-geometry loss. A left-aligned substitute and changed source were rejected by the independent checker.
